Command: No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly
Summary: Deuteronomy 23:3 excludes Ammonites and Moabites from the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation, because they refused Israel bread and water and hired Balaam to curse them.
Commandment: No Ammonite or Moabite shall enter the assembly of the LORD.
Application: Debated: how far these assembly exclusions carry into the church is genuinely disputed — this row does not settle it. Ruth the Moabitess, ancestress of David and of Christ, stands in the discussion.
Purpose: Scripture states the reason: because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee (Deuteronomy 23:4).
Function: A moral law in its traditional classing: it addressed character and conduct within Israel. Deuteronomy 23:3 excludes Ammonites and Moabites from the assembly of the LORD, even to the tenth generation. Its goal was to keep out those who had refused Israel bread and water and hired Balaam to curse them. No particular evil is named here; its work was guarding who stood in the assembly, not restraint.
